holderPosition.legalForm: Ownership of one identified physical bottle, as BAXUS's May 2024 terms describe each collectible NFT; the bottle is kept in BAXUS's own vault
holderPosition.says: Per BAXUS's terms, the NFT is ownership of one bottle that BAXUS keeps in a numbered vault space; it is not a platform token or a fraction. Collecting the bottle needs a redemption, which destroys the NFT, and a delivery subject to age, destination and shipping requirements. The title claim is the operator's own description and has not been tested.

tokens.note: One NFT per bottle, per BAXUS's terms. No individual bottle mint was identified, and the reviewed sources do not name the current token standard, so whether the NFT reader could read it is unknown.

verdict.summary: One NFT for one vaulted bottle is the case v3 was built for: an asset sheet, the vault's holds, an inspection, and a hand-over and receipt on redemption say the holder's position. What v3 cannot show is that the vault and the authenticator are the operator itself, which bottle record prevails, and the insurance. None of the statements is signed for a checked bottle today, and the token standard is not established.
